10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-13b [ED-06, SPK-02 question 3, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — TWO TIMED execution.snapshot EVENTS REACH A REAL BROWSER SEPARATELY, before response closure, through every proxy layer, captured as a HAR from a real browser on the staging hosts. 10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-14 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 4, Platform/SRE (ingress)] — a 15 s HEARTBEAT KEEPS AN IDLE STREAM OPEN across the ingress and any platform proxy, and the EFFECTIVE MAXIMUM STREAM LIFETIME is measured against the intended 60 s. If the effective maximum is BELOW the configured lifetime, the configured value moves to match the measurement and the change is recorded — studioSse.lifetimeSeconds is a §8.5 starting value, not a commitment, and the ingress timeout is derived from it so it moves too. That is the mechanism working, not a criterion failing. Nothing in this repository can measure a proxy it has never crossed.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-15 [ED-06, SPK-02 question 5, Platform/SRE (ingress) + backend dev] — RECONNECT WITH Last-Event-ID TO A DIFFERENT API REPLICA restores the current snapshot. The evidence must show the two connections were served by DIFFERENT PODS: a reconnect that happens to land on the same replica proves nothing and is the way this criterion gets reported passed without being tested. Production runs three replicas scaling to six. The design answers this by reading committed state rather than by affinity, and **NO STICKY-SESSION OR SESSION-AFFINITY SETTING MAY BE INTRODUCED TO MAKE IT PASS** — story 10.18b introduced none, and the streaming Ingress it added carries no affinity annotation of any kind. Trading a design property for a deployment workaround would close this criterion by defeating the thing it exists to check.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-16b [ED-06, SPK-02 questions 1-2, Platform/SRE (ingress) + frontend dev] — THE PLATFORM’S ACTUAL BROWSER-AUTH ROUTE, IN WRITING, COVERING FEDERATED MODE: which route carries the session cookie to the events and video paths — same-origin gateway path, or cross-origin with withCredentials plus exact-origin credentialed CORS — and whether it holds in BOTH standalone and federated (shell-hosted) modes, where the browser’s origin is the PUT platform shell’s and no values file in this chart can know it; and whether a bearer-only requirement exists anywhere on the path, in which case SSE needs the header-capable client inside the centralized API service (STORY 10.11’s, not this one’s) and <video> needs an ambient session regardless. The DEPLOYMENT half is done: exact-origin credentialed CORS compared against the rendered frontend host in the same manifest, never a wildcard, and no credential in any URL. A DEMONSTRATED GATEWAY INCOMPATIBILITY IS A VALID OUTCOME — it selects the documented GET fallback and changes no execution contract.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed ED-06 / SPK-02 — the authenticated route through the real ingress AC-21b [ED-06 / SPK-02 question 7, and ED-02; Platform/SRE + Security] — THE CSRF CONTROL THE PLATFORM ROUTE ACTUALLY PROVIDES, stated in writing by its owner, and whether the application must add one. This story deliberately did NOT enable Spring’s CSRF filter or drop CORS credentials: either changes the public request contract of every existing Checks route, which is not a Studio story’s to land.

10.18b — blocked criteria, recorded as skipped and never passed Staging — the deployed stack under load AC-23b [staging; ED-06/ED-05 and the spikes; Platform/SRE] — KILL SWITCH, DRAIN, RECOVERY AND BOUNDED OVERLOAD OBSERVED AGAINST THE DEPLOYED STACK, with ordinary REST/check service preserved.
